title: A boundary point can disappear
text: This point lies on the edge of the blue disk. But will it still lie on the outside when we combine all the disks?

title: Start with equal-sized disks
text: First, give every disk the same radius. Their top points line up. The highlighted point touches the upper edge of the combined region.

title: Change only the neighboring radii
text: Now let the disks grow toward the right. Keep the blue disk and its old top point fixed. A larger neighbor reaches above that point.

title: Look closely at the old point
text: In this fixed magnified view, the old point is inside the neighboring disk. It is still on its own circle, but it is no longer on the outside of the union.

title: Find the new contact
text: The outer edge now tilts. On the blue disk, its contact moves to the upper left. The yellow arrow marks the outward direction, perpendicular to that edge.

title: Track each contribution
text: Follow the same construction across neighboring disks. Each highlighted contact lies on the same local outer edge. Position and direction belong together.

title: Boundary tracking
text: This local illustration motivates tracking position and outward direction together. A propagated boundary candidate can still lie inside the resulting region.
